keyVerseText: Will he esteem thy riches? no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun מַאֲמָץ (maʼămâts) derives from the root אָמַץ (ʼâmats), which conveys the idea of strength, courage, and steadfastness. This root emphasizes not only physical power but also mental and moral fortitude—being strong, alert, and courageous. Thus, the root meaning of מַאֲמָץ encompasses a dynamic, active strength that is both inward and outward, signifying a force that is established and prevailing.
usageInScripture: The word מַאֲמָץ appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Job 36:19, where it is translated as 'forces' in the phrase 'nor all the forces of strength.' This singular occurrence highlights its meaning as a collective or plural form of strength or power. The consistent translation as 'forces' or 'strength' indicates that מַאֲמָץ conveys not just individual might but also the resources or powers that one might marshal or possess.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מַאֲמָץ as rooted in courageous strength and steadfast power enriches our grasp of divine and human strength in Scripture. It reminds believers that true strength is not merely physical but involves spiritual courage and perseverance grounded in God’s sustaining power. This word invites reflection on the limits of human strength compared to the infinite power of God, encouraging reliance on Him rather than on one’s own resources. In the Christian faith, such a perspective fosters humility and trust in the Lord’s ability to uphold and empower His people beyond what natural strength can achieve.
keyVerseReflection: In Job 36:19, the phrase 'nor all the forces of strength' uses מַאֲמָץ to emphasize that neither riches nor the entirety of human strength can compel God’s favor or esteem. This highlights the insufficiency of human power and resources in influencing divine will. The word מַאֲמָץ here underscores the comprehensive nature of human strength—no matter how great or forceful it may seem, it falls short before God’s sovereign authority, calling believers to depend wholly on Him.
